name: Non-syndromic Unisquamosal Craniosynostosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Non-syndromic Unisquamosal Craniosynostosis

criteria.description: Presence of unilateral skull asymmetry with flattening over the affected squamosal suture region
Radiographic or CT evidence of premature fusion of the squamosal suture without involvement of other sutures
No clinical or genetic evidence of syndromic craniosynostosis or associated systemic anomalies
Normal neurodevelopmental milestones without evidence of increased intracranial pressure

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of unilateral skull asymmetry with radiologic confirmation of isolated squamosal suture fusion and absence of syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of syndromic craniosynostoses and other causes of cranial asymmetry.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral premature fusion of the squamosal suture
searchTerms: early fusion of one squamosal suture
one side squamosal suture closed prematurely
flattened temple bone on one side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Skull asymmetry localized to the squamosal suture region

searchTerms: slight unevenness of one side face
mild facial asymmetry on one side

common.symptomName: Palpable ridging along the affected squamosal suture
searchTerms: ridge felt on affected skull suture

common.symptomName: Absence of increased intracranial pressure signs
searchTerms: no signs of high brain pressure
absence of raised brain pressure signs
small temporal muscle on one side

occasional.symptomName: Mild ipsilateral external auditory canal narrowing
searchTerms: narrow ear canal on one side
slow closing of soft spot on head
epileptic episodes due to skull abnormality

rare.symptomName: Visual disturbances due to orbital involvement
searchTerms: vision problems from eye socket issues
eye disturbances due to orbital involvement
blurred or double vision from eye area

imaging: CT scan showing isolated premature fusion of the squamosal suture
3D cranial reconstruction demonstrating unilateral temporal bone flattening
Absence of fusion in other cranial sutures
genetic: No pathogenic variants associated with syndromic craniosynostosis detected
other: Physical examination revealing unilateral skull asymmetry

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic mutations in FGFR or TWIST genes

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (e.g., vomiting, irritability)
references: Cohen MM Jr. Craniosynostosis: diagnosis, evaluation, and management. 3rd ed. Oxford University Press; 2000.
Wilkie AO, Johnson D, Wall SA. Clinical genetics of craniosynostosis. Curr Opin Pediatr. 2017;29(6):622-628.
